text: IMD reports that India received 713.3 mm of rainfall from 1 June through 23 September 2026, against 837.7 mm normal for the same dates (1971–2020); its displayed departure is −14.9%.

period.cutoff_convention: IMD graphic labels dates June 1 through September 23; clock hour is not specified. Times in this record encode calendar dates only.

method_path: IMD all-India graphic middle and bottom panels; (713.3 / 837.7 - 1) × 100 = −14.85%, rounding to −14.9%.
limitations: Rainfall departure is not a measure of water supply or a drought declaration.
The graphic is a mutable, provider-rounded image; exact region boundaries and station methods were not reconstructed.

text: In an outlook issued 31 August 2026, IMD forecast that all-India rainfall during September was most likely below normal, its category for less than 91% of the 1971–2020 September average. It also identified areas where normal or above-normal rain was possible. This is a dated forecast, not a measured September outcome; check for any later IMD issue.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: Valid only for September 2026 and superseded by any later outlook.
A rainfall forecast is not a water-supply or crop-loss forecast.

text: According to a 31 March 2026 Ministry of Jal Shakti release, the Union Cabinet approved Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 on 10 March and operational guidelines were released on 22 March. The ministry reported releasing ₹1,561.53 crore to five named states for FY 2025–26. This does not establish state expenditure or service outcomes.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: A ministry announcement/release is a single source chain and is not independent treasury confirmation.
The five named states are Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Maharashtra; this is not a drought-specific emergency measure.

text: In a 2 April 2026 parliamentary reply, the Ministry of Jal Shakti said states and Union territories reported tap-water connections for about 15.82 crore of 19.36 crore rural households as of 3 March 2026. Connection counts do not establish regular or safe service.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: This is an administrative count reported by states and UTs, not a household functionality survey.
Rounded headline counts should not be treated as exact household counts.

text: In a national survey conducted July–December 2018, 58.2% of rural and 80.7% of urban households reported a drinking-water facility within their premises.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: Household responses in a 2018 survey; not a 2026 service measure or quality test.
The rural and urban frames differ from later JJM administrative reports.

text: In the same 2018 survey, 87.6% of rural and 90.9% of urban households said their principal source supplied sufficient drinking water throughout the year.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: Self-reported year-round sufficiency from the principal source, not independently measured daily service or safe quality.

text: A July–October 2024 survey of villages already recorded as covered by Jal Jeevan Mission found that 86.5% of surveyed households with taps had received water in the preceding seven days and 83.6% reported supply on their scheme schedule. The report estimated 80.2% met its quantity threshold; 76% of tested household water samples passed its microbiological checks.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: Sampled declared-covered villages, not all rural India; weighted household estimates.
Quantity was estimated using flow at one household per habitation, not each household.
The 76% microbiological sample result is not the share of fully safe or functional households.
The report calculated a separate 76% functionality figure as the minimum of three separately estimated components, not a joint household observation.

text: Karnataka’s 22 September 2026 gazetted order declared 53 additional taluks across 17 districts drought-affected for the 2026 kharif season: 51 severe and two moderate. The order took effect immediately for up to six months unless revoked. It authorizes district authorities to undertake relief under SDRF norms and directs a joint crop-loss survey; it does not establish that aid was delivered or losses measured.

period.cutoff_convention: Order date has calendar precision; 00:00 is a date placeholder, not a signing time.

method_path: Independently counted 53 numbered annex taluks, 51 severe and two moderate, in 17 distinct named districts.
limitations: The order covers listed taluks, not all of Karnataka or India.
It is a declaration and authorization, not proof of relief distribution, crop losses or household water shortage.
Earlier 101- and 23-taluk orders are cited in the gazette but their annexes were not independently reviewed for a cumulative statewide total.

text: In its 10 September 2026 bulletin, the Central Water Commission reported 130.554 billion cubic metres (BCM) of live storage in 178 monitored reservoirs, 70.66% of their combined 184.762 BCM live capacity. This monitored cohort is not all reservoirs or total usable water.

period.cutoff_convention: Bulletin status date is 10 September 2026; 00:00 is a calendar-date placeholder, not a measurement hour.

limitations: CWC monitored-reservoir cohort only; not all storage, groundwater, household supply or river flow.
Status date is 10 September 2026; the newer 17 September bulletin was listed but its official PDF returned 404 on 24 September.
Capacity fill and departure from ten-year normal use different denominators.

text: CWC reported that its 50 monitored southern-region reservoirs held 30.467 BCM on 10 September 2026, 54.52% of their combined 55.879 BCM live capacity and below their corresponding-week ten-year normal of 40.827 BCM. This CWC region is not the same geography as IMD’s South Peninsula rainfall region.

text: In IMD’s completed June–September 2002 South Peninsula (10 subdivisions) series, the four printed monthly totals sum to 466.9 mm, 34.8% below the table’s displayed 1971–2020 normal. This is a rainfall comparison, not evidence that 2026 has reached the same severity.

period.cutoff_convention: Completed calendar months June through September; source values are one-decimal monthly totals, not daily cutoffs.

method_path: Sum IMD printed June, July, August and September monthly totals; (466.9 / 716.1 - 1) × 100 = -34.8% at one decimal.
limitations: Completed June–September seasons cannot be ranked against the current 2026 observation ending 23 September.
The South Peninsula footprint has 10 IMD subdivisions; it is not a set of selected current states.
Brief factual extraction only; do not reproduce the IMD historical table, bulk rows or graphics without a rights decision.

text: In the same IMD completed-season series, South Peninsula rainfall in 2009 summed to 681.6 mm, 4.8% below its displayed 1971–2020 normal, while the all-India total was 709.1 mm, 18.4% below its own displayed normal. National and regional rainfall signals differed that year.

period.cutoff_convention: Completed calendar months June through September; source values are one-decimal monthly totals, not daily cutoffs.

method_path: Sum IMD printed June, July, August and September monthly totals, then (actual / displayed 1971–2020 normal - 1) × 100. South Peninsula 681.6 / 716.1 = -4.8% at one decimal; 2009 India 709.1 / 868.5 = -18.4% at one decimal.
limitations: Completed June–September seasons cannot be ranked against the current 2026 observation ending 23 September.
The South Peninsula footprint has 10 IMD subdivisions; it is not a set of selected current states.
